Connect available skills to demand without turning a scenario into a staffing promise

Give operations, resource, and finance leaders a shared view of utilization, capacity, bench skills, pipeline matches, and capability-building options while keeping assignments and financial commitments under human control.

**Why try it:** A resource manager can ask who is available, see where skills align with demand, and identify the people who need upskilling or an internal innovation path.

## Problem Statement

Professional services leaders need to balance utilization, urgent demand, skill fit, bench cost, and capability development. Manual planning can double-count people, overstate uncertain pipeline, and leave unmatched talent without a deliberate path.

## Solution Summary

Microsoft Copilot Studio provides the planning conversation. Dynamics 365 supplies project and resource context, while Microsoft Teams supports governed staffing and development decisions.

**Blueprint role:** Adds a governed capacity and capability-planning layer across delivery demand, available talent, and workforce investment.

**Capabilities:** Utilization and availability view; Capacity and demand forecast; Bench skill and cost analysis; Pipeline staffing matches; Upskilling and innovation planning. See [responsibilities and trust boundaries](2.Architecture.md).

## Business Outcomes

- Improves shared visibility into skills, availability, and capacity.
- Accelerates evidence-based staffing conversations.
- Supports deliberate upskilling and capability-building decisions.

Claims are qualitative; synthetic demo figures are not customer results or performance commitments. See the [claims policy](../../solutions/README.md#claims-policy).

## Target Users

| Role | Need |
| --- | --- |
| Operations Leader | See firm and level utilization against targets and review capability-building options without approving staffing or benefits. |
| Resource Manager | Compare capacity coming free with weighted pipeline demand and review skill-and-level matches before confirming any staffing. |
| Finance Director | Review bench skills and carrying-cost scenarios without treating opportunity value as booked revenue. |

## In Scope / Out of Scope

### In scope

- Show firm and level utilization against targets, billable and bench headcount and the roster as a synthetic planning snapshot.
- Compare upcoming project endings with pipeline start, duration, probability and requested roles, without assigning anyone.
- Inventory bench consultants, levels, skills and monthly carrying cost; opportunity values remain scenarios.
- Match bench consultants only on exact level and skill, count each person once and keep unmatched resources visible.
- Model upskilling and internal-innovation options with a labeled synthetic payback scenario, separate from approved work.

### Out of scope / approval boundary

- No web search and no live HR or PSA queries; answers use only the two packaged knowledge files.
- No assigning, reserving, deploying, reallocating, hiring, terminating, evaluating or contacting a person.
- No change to employment, project, utilization, training or HR records.
- No approval of training, internal work, client staffing, revenue or financial benefits.
- No pipeline, utilization, revenue or payback scenario described as live, committed, forecast or guaranteed.
- No workshop publishing: validated agents stay in Draft and publication requires explicit confirmation.

## Qualification Checklist

- [ ] Is a Microsoft Copilot Studio target environment, with an approved publisher prefix, available for the resource-planning build?
- [ ] Can the delivery team authenticate with PAC CLI 2.9.3 or newer and initialize a `cli-copilot` project?
- [ ] Has the customer mapped project and resource context to Dynamics 365 and staffing and development review to Microsoft Teams?
- [ ] Are approved, least-privilege Dynamics 365 and Microsoft Teams connections identified, with owners, before the synthetic roster is replaced?
- [ ] Are resource-manager, people-leader, finance, business-owner and leadership approvers named for staffing and capability-building decisions?
- [ ] Will production matching keep both skill and level fit and count each person once in projections?
- [ ] Is publication held for explicit confirmation after replaying RU-01 through RU-05 against the reviewed instructions, knowledge, skills and model?
- [ ] Have governance, telemetry, support and success measures been agreed for production resource planning?

## What Actually Goes Wrong

- **double-counted-consultant:** A consultant is counted more than once in projected utilization.
- **loose-skill-match:** A consultant is matched on skill alone, at the wrong level or beyond the requested count.
- **pipeline-as-committed:** Weighted pipeline or opportunity value is treated as committed work or booked revenue.
- **match-read-as-assignment:** A staffing match is read as an assignment.
- **snapshot-as-live-psa:** The frozen snapshot is presented as a live PSA reading.
- **missing-grounding:** A skill or its knowledge cannot load, but the agent answers from memory.

See [state and recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery).
